description: F-CORE-014: a creation is recorded as a change from nothing (`from: null`), not as an empty diff. The trail was inconsistent about this and nothing noticed: vouchers, fiscal years, dimension types/values and costing runs all wrote `{from: null, to: …}`, while accounts, postings and partners wrote no `changes` at all. `systemDescription` meanwhile published the invariant "every state-changing operation writes an audit record with actor, timestamp, object **and before/after values**" — true of some records and not of others, which is the kind of claim the GoBD census rule exists to stop. The identifying fields only, never a copy of the object: an account's current state is in `accounts`, a partner's in the master data, and an entry's lines are in the journal, which is append-only. A trail that duplicates the object is a second source of truth rather than a history — and for the journal it would double the largest table in the system. What the trail adds is the frame nobody can reconstruct afterwards: when, against which voucher, under which text.

expect.comment: Drei Anlagen, drei Diffs gegen null. `subtype` steht nur beim Konto, das eines hat — ein Feld, das nicht gesetzt wurde, wird nicht als „von null auf null" erfunden.
